samples.summary: changeDecimals steps from the raw stored `dp`, so a NaN `dp` propagates into a new write instead of being clamped
samples.evidence: `const stepped = Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES);` uses `dp` straight from `getActiveDecimalState()`, which returns `style.dp` untouched (sheet.ts:4184). The delta clamps only at format time (`clampDecimals` in formatValue). If the stored `dp` is `NaN` — exactly the hostile/imported value the new clamp exists for — `stepped` is `NaN`, `NaN < 0` is false so `clamped` is false, `target === valueDp` is false, and the function reaches `setRangeStyle({ dp: NaN, ... })`, persisting `NaN` into the style layer. `unsetRangeStyleValues` also can never match it (`NaN !== NaN` → 'conflict'). Every subsequent Increase/Decrease press stays at `NaN` — the control is permanently stuck for that selection — and a NaN is not JSON/CRDT representable, so the value that reaches collaborators is undefined behaviour. Applying `clampDecimals(dp, 2)` before stepping would fix it.

samples.summary: Decrease on an out-of-range stored `dp` (e.g. 400) is a wasted no-op press
samples.evidence: With `dp: 400` the cell renders 20 decimals (clamped in formatValue). `Math.min(400 - 1, 20)` = 20, so the first Decrease writes `dp: 20` and nothing on screen moves; a second press is needed before the user sees anything. Clamping `dp` before adding `delta` (`clampDecimals(dp, 2) + delta`) makes the first press behave. The new test at decimals.test.ts:520 only covers the Increase direction, so this is untested.

samples.summary: selectionRendersAt's new format-aware check makes Decrease reach a write that clobbers a neighbour's number format with `nf: 'number'`
samples.evidence: `if (!nf || nf === 'plain') patch.nf = 'number';` takes `nf` from the ACTIVE cell only, and `setRangeStyle` → `applyStylePatchToExistingCells` (sheet.ts:1978-1991) writes conflicting keys onto each existing cell's own style. So when the active cell has no `nf` and a neighbour has `nf: 'percent'`/`'currency'`, one Decrease silently converts that neighbour to `nf: 'number'` — '0.5' stops reading '50.00%' and reads '0.5'. This delta newly widens the path: `selectionRendersAt` now uses `renderedDecimals`, so selections that previously short-circuited at line 4203 (e.g. plain '12' beside a percent cell storing '12', both 0 decimals by value) now fall through to the write. The new test at decimals.test.ts:504-517 exercises exactly this case and asserts only `dp === 0`, so the lost `nf: 'percent'` on B1 is not caught.

samples.summary: renderedDecimals reports 2 for a currency cell with no `dp`, but formatValue renders the locale/currency default (0 for JPY/KRW)
samples.evidence: `renderedDecimals` returns `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` for every non-plain/non-date format. formatValue's currency branch, when `dp === undefined` (format.ts:198), deliberately omits min/maxFractionDigits and lets Intl use the currency's own default — 0 for JPY/KRW, 3 for some. So for a KRW currency cell showing '₩12', renderedDecimals claims 2 digits, `selectionRendersAt(0)` returns false, and Decrease writes an explicit `dp: 0` (plus, per the finding above, possibly `nf: 'number'`) on a selection that had nothing to drop — the very no-op this guard is supposed to preserve.

mergedFrom.summary: Decrease-decimals no-op guard inspects raw value precision, not the decimals actually rendered, so it silently swallows a legitimate step

finding.summary: Decrease no-op guard (`selectionRendersAt`) inspects only raw values, so a Decrease press does nothing while other selected cells visibly render decimals via their number format
finding.evidence: `changeDecimals` line 4198: `if (stepped < 0 && !explicitDp && (await this.selectionRendersAt(0))) return;`. `selectionRendersAt` (4246-4261) only looks at `cell.v` via `decimalsInValue`, never at the cell's effective `nf`/`dp`. Scenario: A1 = '12' plain (active, valueDp 0, no explicit dp) and B1 = '12' with `nf: 'number'` (renders '12.00'). Selecting A1:B1 and pressing Decrease returns early — B1 keeps showing two decimals even though it has decimals to drop. The comment on the guard explicitly claims the check "has to look past the active cell: a neighbour that still shows decimals has something to lose", but a neighbour that shows decimals only because of its format is missed.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that `selectionRendersAt` "only looks at `cell.v` via `decimalsInValue`, never at the cell's effective `nf`/`dp`" — is not true of this repository. At sheet.ts:4262-4263 the helper resolves each cell's effective style via `resolveEffectiveStyle(ref.r, ref.c, cell.s)` and compares `renderedDecimals(value, effective)`, not `decimalsInValue(value)`. `renderedDecimals` (format.ts:152-161) returns `decimalsInValue` only for `plain`/`date`/no format and returns `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` for every numeric format, so a cell storing '12' under `nf: 'number'` with no `dp` reports 2 rendered decimals. Walking the reviewer's exact scenario: A1 plain '12' -> 0, B1 '12' with `nf: 'number'` -> 2, so the loop returns false at 4264, `selectionRendersAt(0)` is false, the early return at sheet.ts:4203 is not taken, and the explicit write at sheet.ts:4240 steps B1 to zero decimals. `decimalsInValue` appears in this file only at sheet.ts:4180 inside `getActiveDecimalState` (computing `valueDp`), not in the guard. The scenario is additionally covered by the existing test 'should step a neighbour whose decimals come from its format' (decimals.test.ts:486-500), which constructs exactly A1 plain + B1 `nf: 'number'` and asserts B1 drops to zero decimals after Decrease.

finding.summary: `unsetKeepsRendering` formats every selected cell with the ACTIVE cell's `nf`, ignoring each cell's own effective format, so an unset can be approved that changes another cell's rendering
finding.evidence: Lines 4290-4296 compute `effective = this.resolveEffectiveStyle(...)` but use only `effective?.cu`; the comparison uses the active cell's `nf`/`nfAfter` for every cell. If the active cell has `dp` with plain/undefined `nf` (nf param undefined → both sides return the raw value, always equal) while a neighbour carries `nf: 'percent'` (or 'currency') with the same stored `dp`, the check passes and `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp})` strips that neighbour's `dp` (its style verdict is 'match' since only `dp` is requested). The neighbour then falls back to the format's default 2 decimals instead of the requested `target`, so the step silently renders it wrong (e.g. target 3 → neighbour still shows 2).

verdict.reason: The finding's core mechanism is not present in the code. `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4289-4317) does NOT use the active cell's `nf` for every cell: it resolves each cell's effective style at line 4302 and reads that cell's own format at line 4304 (`const nf = effective?.nf;`), using it on both sides of the comparison at lines 4309-4310. The active cell's `nf` is not in scope — the function only receives `removeNf: boolean` and `target: number` (4289-4292), with the caller passing `nf === 'number'` (4220). Replaying the reviewer's exact scenario: active cell plain ⇒ `removeNf = false`; for a neighbour with `nf: 'percent'`, line 4307 yields `nfAfter = 'percent'` (unchanged, since `nf !== 'number'`), so line 4309 compares `formatValue(v,'percent',undefined)` — 2 decimals via `clampDecimals(dp, 2)` at format.ts:182/22-30 — against `formatValue(v,'percent',target=3)` — 3 decimals. These differ, so the function returns false and `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp})` at sheet.ts:4231 is never reached; control falls through to the explicit write at sheet.ts:4236-4240. The same per-cell logic covers the 'currency' case (format.ts:195-210, where absent `dp` gives the format's own default). `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:879-890) merges `nf` across sheet/col/row/range/cell layers, so the per-cell format is genuinely available and used. The claimed data-corruption path is precisely what this check rejects.
